correctness.rationale: The primary fine harmonic triple (k,pi1,pi2) represents v=(pi1^{-1}+e_k,pi2^{-1}+e_k) with each coordinate sum C_n=n(n+1)/2+1. Define mu=C_n/n. The permutation centered square-sum is n(n^2-1)/12 in each block; cross terms depend only on the positions p,q of k. From three allowed before/after classes a,b,c with a+b+c=n-1 we get p+q=n+1+b. This yields exactly d^2=n(n^2-1)/6+2(n-1)/n+2b. The published class count n*multinomial(n-1;a,b,c)*(a+b)!c!a!(b+c)! sums algebraically to M_{n,b}. Taking b=n-1 gives R^2 as stated and n((n-1)!)^2 outer vertices. Those vertices have exact barycenter c_n=(mu 1,mu 1); average squared distance from another center Q is R^2+||Q-c_n||^2, proving unique smallest enclosing sphere. Independently enumerated all fine triples for n=2,3,4 with exact Fractions, reproducing counts (4,2), (30,24,12), (384,384,288,144), radius progression and outer barycenter. Finite enumeration is corroboration; symbolic proof handles arbitrary n.
residual_risks: The metric depends on the exact standard 2n-coordinate embedding; an affine-equivalent polytope would not preserve radii.
The fine triple exclusion of a label after k in both permutations is necessary to p+q=n+1+b.

value.rationale: The n-shell stratification and exact multiplicities are a natural, all-rank radial invariant of a named combinatorial polytope. The order statistic b controls Euclidean radius by a universal gap of 2, while the complete outer contact class and unique minimum sphere give a usable sharp metric boundary. This supplies meaningful geometric information not determined by total vertex counts or the previously published inradius; the proof is self-contained given canonical vertex coordinates.
residual_risks: It does not compute pairwise distances, ellipsoids or vertex distribution under another affine embedding.

final_claim: For n>=2 the standard Ardila-Escobar harmonic polytope H_{n,n} has exactly n centered vertex shells with squared radii n(n^2-1)/6+2(n-1)/n+2b for b=0..n-1, explicit counts M_{n,b}=n!/b! sum_{r=b}^{n-1} r!(n+b-1-r)!, and unique minimum enclosing sphere R_n^2=(n^2-1)(n^2+12)/(6n), contacted only when the marked index is last in both permutations.
limitations: No assertion about all nonvertex boundary points lying on radial shells.
Mathematical priority is best-of-knowledge, with other embeddings/metric terminology a residual risk.
